token.description: GitHub token the agent uses for the repos above. Usually ${env:GITHUB_TOKEN}.

github.title: GitHub
github.description: Read repositories, issues, and pull requests. With write access, open branches and pull requests.

url.description: GitLab address. Change it for self-managed GitLab.

token.description: GitLab token the agent uses for the projects above. Usually ${env:GITLAB_TOKEN}.

gitlab.title: GitLab
gitlab.description: Read projects, issues, and merge requests. With write access, open branches and merge requests.

docker.title: Docker
docker.description: Inspect images and containers. With write access, build images for the ship flow.

namespaces.description: Namespaces the agent may access. Nothing outside them.

databases.description: Database workloads to watch on the console Overview, as namespace/name (a StatefulSet or Deployment). The namespace must be in the list above. For databases outside the cluster, or to check the database itself, use the Databases connector.

kubeconfig.description: Kubeconfig for the cluster. Not needed when the agent runs inside the cluster with its own service account. Usually ${env:KODRA_KUBECONFIG}.

kubernetes.title: Kubernetes
kubernetes.description: Inspect workloads in EKS, AKS, GKE, or on-prem clusters. With write access, scale deployments.

github-actions.title: GitHub Actions
github-actions.description: Read workflow runs and logs. With write access, propose pipeline changes through pull requests.

gitlab-ci.title: GitLab CI
gitlab-ci.description: Read pipelines and job logs. With write access, propose pipeline changes through merge requests.

username.description: Jenkins user the API token belongs to.

jobs.description: Jobs the agent may work with, by full name. A folder covers every job under it.

jenkins.title: Jenkins
jenkins.description: Read Jenkins jobs, builds, and console logs. With write access, stop a build after approval.

azure-devops.title: Azure DevOps
azure-devops.description: Read Azure Pipelines runs and logs.

bitbucket.title: Bitbucket
bitbucket.description: Read Bitbucket Pipelines runs and logs.

alertmanagerUrl.description: Alertmanager address. Leave empty to read alerts from Prometheus.

pollIntervalSeconds.description: How often to check for firing alerts, in seconds.

bearerToken.description: Bearer token, only if your Prometheus requires one. Usually ${env:PROMETHEUS_TOKEN}.

prometheus.title: Prometheus
prometheus.description: Query metrics and watch firing alerts. Read-only.

grafana.title: Grafana
grafana.description: Read dashboards, and logs from Loki through Grafana. Read-only.

services.description: AWS services the agent can read: eks, cloudwatch. Each one adds tools the model reads on every question, so leave out what you do not need.

aws.title: AWS
aws.description: Read EKS clusters and CloudWatch metrics, logs, and alarms. Read-only.

host.description: Host name or IP address, as seen from the agent (or from the tunnel host).

port.description: Port. Leave empty for the engine default (3306 or 5432).

database.description: Database to connect to. PostgreSQL uses postgres when empty.

password.description: The database user’s password. A secret reference.

tls.description: Encryption: verify (encrypted, certificate checked), require (encrypted, certificate not checked), or off.

tunnelHost.description: SSH tunnel: the bastion host to connect through. Leave empty to connect directly.

tunnelPort.description: SSH tunnel: the bastion’s SSH port.

tunnelUser.description: SSH tunnel: the user on the bastion.

tunnelHostKey.description: SSH tunnel: the bastion’s host key fingerprint. The tunnel is refused if it does not match. Get it with: ssh-keyscan bastion | ssh-keygen -lf -

tunnelKey.description: SSH tunnel: the private key for the bastion user. A secret reference.

maxLagSeconds.description: A replica this many seconds behind is not fully healthy.

connectionsWarnPercent.description: Connections in use, as a percentage of the maximum, at which the database is not fully healthy.

databases.description: The databases to watch. Use a database user that can only read.

databases.title: Databases
databases.description: Watch the databases you list, wherever they run: standalone, in the cloud (like Amazon RDS), or in Kubernetes. MariaDB, MySQL, and PostgreSQL, directly or through an SSH tunnel. Health checks only.

azure.title: Microsoft Azure
azure.description: Read Azure resources, AKS, and Azure Monitor.

gcp.title: Google Cloud
gcp.description: Read Google Cloud resources, GKE, and Cloud Monitoring.

channel.description: Channel for alerts, summaries, and approvals.

botToken.description: Slack bot token. Starts with xoxb-. Usually ${env:SLACK_BOT_TOKEN}.

appToken.description: Slack app-level token for Socket Mode. Starts with xapp-. Usually ${env:SLACK_APP_TOKEN}.

slack.title: Slack
slack.description: Talk to the agent and approve its actions in Slack. Uses Socket Mode, so no public endpoint is needed.

teams.title: Microsoft Teams
teams.description: Talk to the agent and approve its actions in Teams.

approvals.description: Who approves write actions, and how long a request stays valid.

items.description: Namespaces and repositories with their own approval rules.

limits.description: Limits for each question the agent answers, and a monthly budget.

console.description: The web console: status, activity, usage, chat, and approvals.

network.description: Proxy and CA certificates for every outbound connection.

dataProtection.description: Customer data masked before anything leaves the agent.

metrics.description: The agent's own Prometheus metrics: counts and durations, never content.

tracing.description: OpenTelemetry traces of turns, model calls, and tool calls.
